thread:
maria: Heads-up — our audit logs for `role.update` events around 08:12 UTC today have multiple records with `actor: null`. Compliance spotted it in the weekly check. Anyone seen this pattern?
aj: I noticed a couple while chasing token-rotation noise. The principal_resolver is returning null for some requests.
maria: example payload I pulled:
```json
{"event":"role.update","role":"billing_admin","actor":null,"request_id":"req_12ab34","ts":"2026-03-20T08:12:11Z"}
```
olivia: I also saw a follow-up from the pipeline for the same req id: `audit:processed req_12ab34 -> anonymized` — sounds like a post-ingest redaction step.
security-bot: Automod: redaction policy `PII_SCRUB` applied to request_id=req_12ab34; fields redacted: ["user_email","actor"] (policy id=5)
sam: Wait, we should NOT be stripping `actor` for admin permission changes. That's required for SOX/compliance. Was this a ruleset change?
aj: We onboarded the KMS-backed audit encryptor last week. During a decryption error path we currently emit the record with `actor=null` to avoid partial plaintext. Looks like some older logs hit that path.
maria: That's a compliance gap. Compliance requires an auditable actor for privilege changes. We can't lose that info. What's our mitigation?
olivia: Legal reminded us we can't store unencrypted PII. We could instead persist a non-reversible `actor_hash` (sha256) in plaintext for correlation, and keep the full actor encrypted. That preserves linkage without cleartext PII.
aj: Agreed. Proposal: change the encryptor to always write these fields: `request_id`, `actor_hash`, `encrypted_payload`. On decrypt failure we still have `actor_hash` and can correlate to other logs. Also add a `actor_missing:true` flag so auditors know it was degraded.
sam: Backfill plan: correlate request_id -> gateway access logs -> grpc auth headers to recover the principal. I can run the backfill job. Steps: 1) export request_ids with actor=null 2) join to gateway logs by request_id and timestamp 3) write recovered_actor_hash into audit index and produce CSV for compliance. I can take ownership.
maria: Please open a compliance ticket and include expected deliverables: CSV with recovered actor_hashes, list of affected role changes, timeline, and evidence (raw logs + backfill transform). We need initial backlog within 72h.
aj: Created SEC-3421 in the tracker, assigned to @sam, due Fri EOD, severity: high. Added note: preserve encrypted bucket objects, do not modify originals.
olivia: Also: add CI acceptance test that simulates KMS decrypt failure and asserts `actor_hash` present and `actor_missing:true`, and that the redaction policy doesn't silently drop actor_hash.
security-bot: Incidentbot: created incident-2026-03-20-actor-null (P2). Notified on-call and compliance.
sam: I'll start exporting the list now and post progress in this thread. If anyone has an index of request_id -> kube-pod mapping that would help (some records cross-project).
maria: pinging @eng-infra for mapping: we need the request_id -> pod/container table (last 30 days). Also tag @compliance for the regulatory check.
aj: Quick temporary mitigation: add a middleware to surface a warning metric when `actor:null` and increment a gauge `audit.actor_missing.count` so we can alert if rate spikes. I'll add that in the next deploy.
olivia: One more thing — check our retention policy on audit S3: compliance wants untouched originals for 12 months; do not re-encrypt in-place. Backfill should write a separate findings index.
maria: OK. Standup in 10 to align owners and timeline. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
